newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal turns higher on commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal turns higher on commercial buying.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures turned higher early, lifted by aggressive commercial buying, pit sources said.

Soyoil was also up on spillover strength from soybeans which posted gains early on fund buying. That market had been braced for selling after funds dumped 25 million bushels on Wednesday, contributing to limit losses.

Exports drew mixed reviews. USDA on Thursday put weekly net soymeal export sales at 30,000 tonnes, at the low end of expectations for 30,000 to 75,000 tonnes. Soyoil sales of 1,900 tonnes were above expectation.
New crop sales were also said to be strong.
In opening trade, Term Commodities bought 900 lots July soymeal which lent a firm tone to that contract.
At 1004 CDT, soymeal was up $1.90 to $0.20 per ton with July up $0.20 at $273.30. Soyoil was up 0.11 to 0.02 cent per lb with July up 0.02 at 23.36.
